rules.text: If the chart's x-axis category labels bind to the form's option labels and the y-axis 'Value' scale is comparable to the printed percentage labels, then the category with the highest printed percentage label is the category with the highest current labeled rating share.
rules.conditions: The chart's category labels must match the form's option labels, and the printed percentage labels must be the authoritative 'labeled rating share' values.

rules.text: If the task requires selecting the category with the highest current labeled rating share, and the chart shows Design at 52%, Support at 45%, Delivery at 39%, Other at 32%, Quality at 24%, and Price at 10%, then Design is the category with the highest current labeled rating share.
rules.conditions: The printed percentage labels are the 'labeled rating share' values, and the task's 'highest' refers to the maximum of these values.

rules.text: If the form's primary field 'Product feedback follow-up category' requires selecting the category with the highest current labeled rating share, and the chart shows Design at 52% as the highest, then the correct action is to select 'Select Design'.
rules.conditions: The form's primary field is the one that must be filled based on the chart's highest rating share, and the option 'Select Design' corresponds to the 'Design' category.

observations.content: The x-axis is labeled 'Category' and has tick labels: Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other.
The y-axis is labeled 'Value' and has tick marks from 0 to 55 in increments of 5.
There are six blue circular data points, one above each x-axis category label.
The data points have printed percentage labels: 24% (Quality), 10% (Price), 52% (Design), 45% (Support), 39% (Delivery), 32% (Other).

chains.claim: The chart's x-axis labels (Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other) include the form's option labels (Design, Quality, Support). The y-axis 'Value' scale and the printed percentage labels (e.g., 52% for Design) are consistent, indicating that the printed labels are the 'labeled rating share' values. Therefore, the category with the highest printed percentage label is the category with the highest current labeled rating share.

task_evidence.content: Select the category with the highest current labeled rating share

chains.claim: Comparing the printed percentage labels: 52% (Design) > 45% (Support) > 39% (Delivery) > 32% (Other) > 24% (Quality) > 10% (Price). Design has the highest value (52%), so it is the category with the highest current labeled rating share.

observations.content: The printed percentage label for the 'Design' category is 52%, which is the highest among all categories.

chains.claim: The form's primary field 'Product feedback follow-up category' requires selecting the category with the highest current labeled rating share. The chart shows Design at 52% as the highest. The form option 'Select Design' corresponds to the 'Design' category. Therefore, the correct action is to select 'Select Design'.
